title: EV charging for fleets: depot, office and drivers’ homes | VOOL
description: Charge a fleet on the connection you have, see cost per vehicle, and reimburse drivers who charge company cars at home.

sections.title: One system for the depot, the office and the driver’s home
sections.lead: Charge the fleet on the connection you already have, see the cost of every vehicle, and reimburse home charging by the exact kWh.

items.title: At the depot
items.text: Vehicles return together and leave in the morning. The LMC spreads charging over the night so the depot connection is enough.

items.title: At the office
items.text: Company cars, employees’ own cars and visitors on the same chargers, each with its own price and report.

items.title: At the driver’s home
items.text: The driver gets a VOOL charger at home. Company charging is reported by the kWh, private charging stays separate.

items.title: Cost per vehicle and driver
items.text: Energy and cost for every session, by RFID card or app user.

items.title: Reports on a schedule
items.text: Monthly reports for accounting and for reimbursing drivers.

items.title: Live status
items.text: Which vehicles are charging, which are full and which charger needs attention.

items.title: Cheapest hours
items.text: Charging follows electricity prices where the schedule allows.

items.title: Any OCPP charger
items.text: Add existing chargers from other makers to the same portal.

items.title: Open to the public
items.text: Depot chargers that stand idle in the daytime can earn money from other drivers.

sections.title: Plug in at six. Charging starts when prices drop.
sections.text: The car waits through the evening price peak and charges in the cheapest hours of the night. It is ready at the time you set.
sections.note: Example hourly prices in ct/kWh, not live data.

items.title: Omniva: 300 chargers for couriers
items.text: Chargers across Estonia over five years for the courier fleet, starting in Tallinn, Tartu, Kuressaare and Rakvere.

items.title: Hansabuss: electric buses at existing hubs
items.text: Charging at Latvian hubs and at drivers’ homes without major changes to the infrastructure.

items.q: How do we reimburse drivers who charge at home?
items.a: The driver’s charger reports each session. You get the kWh per driver and reimburse at the rate you agree. In some countries, Germany for example, reimbursement must be by the exact kWh.

items.q: Do all vehicles need to be the same make?
items.a: No. VOOL charges any electric vehicle with a Type 2 connection.
Send us the main fuse size and the number of vehicles. With load management most depots charge overnight without an upgrade.

items.q: Can drivers also use public chargers?
items.a: Yes, at VOOL public chargers with the VOOL App. Roaming with other networks is being added.

sections.title: How many vehicles fit on your depot connection?
sections.lead: Send the number of vehicles, their return and departure times and the main fuse size.
